reviews.title: Absolutely spectacular
reviews.comment: Now, let it be known that I am not an audiophile. I don't do a great deal of music listening, and I don't thrive on audio devices. My knowledge of audio is (maybe) a bit above average, but I'm no guru or specialist/expert. However, I am fully aware of how devices compare to others I've tried. The responsiveness of this headset if far and away the best performing device I've used in recent memory. The inline controls respond immediately, even on my bogged-down corporate laptop. I can't believe how light weight and comfortable this device is. The sound is crystal clear, and the noise cancellation needs to be heard to be believed. For a unit that does not completely cover the outer ear, I am not bothered, at all, by the sounds of a busy lab around me. For the price, this headset is an excellent value, and I highly recommend them to anyone that requires a set for business purposes. I have not used them for entertainment, so I can't offer an opinion in that respect. For daily use at work, however, they are without compare

reviews.title: The perfect web conference headset!
reviews.comment:
I have just finished testing my new Sennheiser SC 60s, the sixth headset I have purchased in two years, and (at least on day one) they are far and away the best I've ever purchased for under $40. Specifically:
* In music playback, they have a subjectively full-frequency response (caveat, this was not evaluated with equipment and, like everyone over 25 I do not have full-frequency hearing).
* Sound isolation is moderate, as expected from on-ear rather than over-ear headphones. I wouldn't use these for high-fidelity music reproduction.
* Voice recording quality, when mic boom is positioned just outside outer corner of the mouth, was excellent both for recording and over a JoinMe web conference.
* Microphone noise cancellation is outstanding. During playback of a voice recording made three feet away from a fan, voice was clear, but close listening was necessary to hear the sound of the fan. Recording while one foot from the fan, with wind noise plainly audible during the recording, was reduced at playback to just a mild and undistracting sound audible behind the clear voice.
* Microphone directionality permitted loud typing away on a noisy keyboard to be only barely audible behind a clear voice during playback.
* Comfort is good. These headphones sit gently on the ear, but I would not want to wear them all day.
* Compatibility: Headset was instantly recognized by Windows 10 computer; no other platform tested.
Caveat: While these are the best headphones I have ever used for web conferencing, I don't know how long these qualities will hold up over time. I plan to update this evaluation in a year.
Hello all, this is me 5 years later (apologies if you've been waiting the previous 4 years for my follow-up ;). The reviewed Sennheisers lasted 4 years before almost daily use caused the wire casing to fray just below the ear cups. They still worked perfectly, but I replaced them since a reliable headset is vital in my work. This set is just as good as the last, and I have recommended them to many clients in online teaching. To be honest—but please don't share this with Sennheiser—they'd probably be the best you could buy at US$80. The fact that they are only $40 is quite remarkable.
reviews.author: Dean Earlix

reviews.title: It's not the high quality Sennheiser I grew to like and Ear pieces held together by cheap foam
reviews.comment:
I bought this thinking Sennheiser is worth spending a little more for higher quality but wow it's not. It works well with Microsoft Teams through a VPN, but it's not exactly nice feeling. Ear foam is cheap and rough feeling compared to my Plantronics C3220, audio feels good, they can hear me through a VPN, but a couple concerns
- It's all plastic and foam, so it doesn't conform to my head and puts slight but consistent pressure on my ears.
- The foam behind the ear piece holds it together, other $30-40 headsets haven't had this.
- It's made by Epos but with the Sennheiser name only because it has their usb drivers
reviews.author: Ben P.

reviews.title: This is the perfect conference call headset-and I've tried a lot of them
reviews.comment:
I bought my first pair of Sennheisers about 5 years ago. The quality is so good I also record a podcast on it. I am on Zoom as the CEO of a services company some 6-8 hours a day-both before and during the pandemic.
I have since issued these headphones to anyone in my company who needs a pair.  They're phenomenal. And it's not just "good for the price" -- recently the foam earpads got just so worn out I set out to see if I could "upgrade."
I tried every one of Wirecutter's picks and none of them had the mic quality this one does for the price.  It absolutely kills background noise (all but the worst of it). Think gas powered lawn mowers, dryers, etc.  the boom is adjustable too. I wear glasses and the headset doesn't hurt my ears after being worn for hours.  I've also really abused these things, thrown them in backpacks for travel without a case, and they just keep going.  if Sennheiser wold just sell me some foam ear pads I'd probably just replace those.  This thing is THAT good.
I tried headsets that cost 10x what this costs--and the mic quality was nowhere as good.  Those other headsets also don't let you wear the mic on the left side if you wish, nor do they have a cord that's as long as this one, with an inline control.  I like being able to mute with a button on the line vs fiddling with my headset on a video call. It's distracting to people.
On top of it, I don't look like an air traffic controller because the ear pieces are not large. Even music from my laptop sounds just fine.
I really did try to replace these with something "better"- but in the end, I couldn't do it. I tried to spend a lot more money but nothing was as good as these.
It almost never happens anymore that you get a great product at such a great price.  Thanks, Sennheiser!
I don't know how they can do this for the price, but I'm glad they can.
